+From 7053d49af0f48a80698c6736958abe92ee21ac69 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
+From: Viktor Pashaiev <w.paszajew@gmail.com>
+Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 08:45:55 +0200
+Subject: [PATCH] auth-options: only serialise placeholder strings when option
+ is non-NULL in untrusted mode
+
+When authenticating in untrusted mode, sshauthopt_serialise() unconditionally
+serialised "true" for force_command and "yes" for cert_principals regardless
+of whether the option was actually set.
+
+This caused the unprivileged child process to deserialise force_command as
+a valid non-NULL string even when no forced-command was configured on the
+key. Under configurations like PermitRootLogin=forced-commands-only + UsePAM=yes,
+the child considered root login accepted for forced-command and proceeded with
+PAM account management (MONITOR_REQ_PAM_ACCOUNT / msg 102). The privileged
+monitor rejected the root login because its actual force_command was NULL,
+causing a fatal assertion:
+"fatal: monitor_child_preauth: unexpected authentication from 102"
+
+Fix this by only serialising "true" or "yes" if the corresponding option field
+is non-NULL.
+
+Bug-Ubuntu: https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/openssh/+bug/2166842
+Forwarded: https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/pull/712
+---
+ auth-options.c | 6 ++++--
+ 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
+
+diff --git a/auth-options.c b/auth-options.c
+index 4bbddd7ba..381f64739 100644
+--- a/auth-options.c
++++ b/auth-options.c
+@@ -823,9 +823,11 @@ sshauthopt_serialise(const struct sshauthopt *opts, struct sshbuf *m,
+ 
+ 	/* String options; these may be NULL */
+ 	if ((r = serialise_nullable_string(m,
+-	    untrusted ? "yes" : opts->cert_principals)) != 0 ||
++	    (untrusted && opts->cert_principals != NULL) ?
++	    "yes" : opts->cert_principals)) != 0 ||
+ 	    (r = serialise_nullable_string(m,
+-	    untrusted ? "true" : opts->force_command)) != 0 ||
++	    (untrusted && opts->force_command != NULL) ?
++	    "true" : opts->force_command)) != 0 ||
+ 	    (r = serialise_nullable_string(m,
+ 	    untrusted ? NULL : opts->required_from_host_cert)) != 0 ||
+ 	    (r = serialise_nullable_string(m,
+-- 
+2.43.0
